restatements.text: Requires all county jails to honor federal immigration detainer requests by holding the named individuals for up to 48 hours beyond their normal release time.

evidence.quote: Every county jail shall honor a detainer request from federal immigration authorities by holding the named person for up to 48 hours after the person would otherwise be released.
evidence.why: It creates a new state mandate requiring local county jails to detain individuals for federal authorities.

analysis.answer: Under current law, each county decides whether its jail honors federal immigration detainers. The measure changes this by mandating that all county jails honor these requests, holding named individuals for up to 48 hours past their normal release time.

The direct cost includes the daily expense of housing, feeding, and supervising inmates for an additional 48 hours. Counties may also face legal costs or liability if individuals sue over being held past their lawful release date on a civil detainer.

County governments bear the financial burden of the extra detention time. Federal immigration authorities benefit by having more time to assume custody of individuals directly from jails without needing to locate them in the community.

Federal authorities will likely take custody of more individuals directly from county jails. Some immigrants and their family members may become less likely to report crimes or interact with local police if they fear such contact will result in detention and deportation.

The text addresses the problem of federal immigration authorities lacking the time to take custody of individuals before they are released from local jails. The mechanism reaches this by establishing a mandatory 48-hour hold period statewide.

Federal immigration authorities gain discretion over who is held by local jails. State government gains power over local county governments, which lose the discretion to set their own detainer policies.

Researchers disagree about the effects of local immigration enforcement on community safety. Some studies find that honoring detainer requests reduces crime by removing offenders, while other studies find no effect on crime rates and conclude that it deters immigrant communities from reporting crimes or cooperating with local police.

flags.quote: Every county jail shall honor a detainer request from federal immigration authorities by holding the named person for up to 48 hours
flags.note: The measure requires county jails to hold individuals for up to 48 additional hours but does not provide state funding to cover the costs of the extended detention.
